newsitem.title: USA: Senator proposes to scrap U.S. income tax.
newsitem.headline: Senator proposes to scrap U.S. income tax.

text.p: Republican Sen. Richard Lugar launched a new effort Tuesday to reform the federal tax system, proposing legislation to scrap income, estate and gift taxes along with the Internal Revenue Service.

In their place, the Indiana senator called for a national sales tax, saying taxing consumption would encourage savings and investment. He made tax reform a central part of his short-lived campaign for the Republican presidential nomination last year, backing a 17 percent retail sales tax and abolition of the income, capital gains, gift and inheritance taxes and elimination of the tax-collecting IRS.

Lugar said he would file a Senate bill Tuesday to repeal the estate and gift taxes along with a resolution to eliminate the federal income tax and replace it with a consumption tax. A bill would be filed later to enact the sales tax, which would be the first such Senate bill, an aide said.
If estate and gift taxes could not be repealed, Lugar said he would focus on removing them from farms and small businesses by creating a $5 million exemption.
"The estate tax -- far higher than income or capital gains rates -- forces many family-owned farms and businesses to sell to larger corporations," he said in a statement.

"A single-rate consumption tax on goods and services is the fundamental change needed to spur economic growth and increase wages, savings and investment ... A sales tax would be collected at the retail level, allowing us to abolish the IRS."
Lugar would file his legislation without cosponsors, an aide said, but he pointed to similar tax reform ideas percolating in the House.
